look.animateHint: Widgets fade in and glide when they move. Your site setting for motion still counts.

layout.columnsHint: Widgets are placed on these columns; changing the number scales nothing, so widgets may need a new size.
layout.gravityHint: On: free space above a widget closes up by itself. Off: widgets stay exactly where you drop them, gaps and all.
layout.phoneAuto: The phone layout is made from the desktop one. Press Edit on a phone to arrange it yourself.
layout.phoneOwn: You arranged the phone layout yourself.
layout.phoneReset: Make it from the desktop layout again
layout.boardHelp_one: {{count}} widget on {{pages}} page(s). Press Edit on the page to move, resize and add widgets.
layout.boardHelp_other: {{count}} widgets on {{pages}} page(s). Press Edit on the page to move, resize and add widgets.
layout.refreshHint_normal: Widgets fetch new data on their own schedule (weather every 30 min, prices every 5 min, …) while the tab is visible.
layout.refreshHint_slow: A third as often: less traffic, for slow connections or rate-limited services.
layout.refreshHint_open: Only when the page opens (if the last data is old) or when you refresh a widget yourself.
layout.shortcutsHint: E: edit the board · /: search · Alt + 1–9: pages · Ctrl + ,: Customize. Turn them off if they get in the way.

search.newTab: Open results in a new tab

iconProviderHints.auto: DuckDuckGo's icon service first, then the site's own icon. Sharp enough and private: the service only sees the site's name.
iconProviderHints.duckduckgo: icons.duckduckgo.com: sees only the site's name, not you.
iconProviderHints.google: Google's favicon service: the sharpest icons; Google sees which sites are on your dash.

iconProviderHints.none: Only the first letter of each site, nothing is loaded.

help.intro: Integrations connect the dash to your services, like in Homarr. Add one here, then pick it in a widget's settings; one integration can feed several widgets.
help.navidrome: Use your Navidrome login (a separate user with few rights is a good idea).
help.github: A fine-grained token with read-only access to “Contents” and “Metadata” of the repositories you want is enough.
help.gitlab: A personal access token with the read_api scope.
help.gitea: Without a token only public repositories work. Settings → Applications → a token with read access to repositories.
help.pihole: Pi-hole 6: the web password or an app password. Pi-hole 5: the API token (Settings → API).
help.homeassistant: Your profile → Security → Long-lived access tokens.
help.uptimekuma: The part after /status/ in the status page's address.
help.glances: Run Glances in web server mode (glances -w); a login only if you set one.
help.custom: Widgets then ask for paths under this address (e.g. v1/stats).
help.plex: Your X-Plex-Token (Plex: open an item's XML and copy the token from the address).
help.audiobookshelf: Settings → Users → your user → API token.
help.immich: Account settings → API keys → New API key.
help.webdav: The address of the share; a user name and password only if it needs one.
help.copyparty: Only the password (copyparty logins have no user name).
help.nextcloud: Use an app password (Settings → Security → Devices & sessions).
help.portainer: Your user → Access tokens. Leave the environment empty for the first one.
help.gotify: A client token (Clients → Create client), not an app token.
help.ntfy: Topics are read with your token, if your server needs one.
help.proxmox: Datacenter → Permissions → API tokens (read-only is enough). The server needs a trusted certificate.
help.speedtest: An API token from your profile (newer versions); without one the open endpoint is tried.

intro.title: Everything you check every day, on one page.
intro.lead: The search bar above already works for everyone: search the web, convert, calculate and look things up as you type. Log in and this page becomes your own dash, with widgets on a grid you arrange, your own look, and the same setup on every device.

widgets.title: Over 40 widgets
widgets.text: Weather, calendar, bookmarks, feeds, releases, to-dos, notes, calculator, music and more, sized and placed the way you like.

search.title: A search bar that answers
search.text: Currencies, units, time zones, encodings, QR codes, passwords, your IP: type it and it's there. Try “help”.

sync.title: Synced on every device
sync.text: Log in anywhere and your dash is there, exactly as you left it. Changes from two devices are merged.

integrations.title: Your services, connected
integrations.text: Jellyfin, Navidrome, Immich, Home Assistant, Pi-hole, GitHub and many more, with their keys kept safely on the server.

look.title: Looks the way you want
look.text: Colours, backgrounds, fonts, card styles, pages and your own CSS. Keep it minimal or fill it up.

private.title: No tracking
private.text: No ads and no profiling. What you put on your dash is only used to show it to you.

intro.login: Log in to make it yours
intro.galleryNote: Log in to add them to your own dash.
intro.note: Free. You sign up with Discord; email login can be added later.
